messages:
Morgan: Quick heads up — I found a bunch of KMS wrap/unwrap operations in Cloud Audit Logs that don't match any currently-active service accounts. Looks like orphaned grants from an older partner integration.

Raj: Can you paste the query you used?

Morgan: Sure — I filtered by cryptoKeyName and timeframe. Example:```gcloud logging read \"resource.type=cloud_kms_crypto_key AND protoPayload.methodName=(\'google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.AsymmetricSign\' OR \'google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Encrypt\') AND timestamp>\"2025-11-01T00:00:00Z\"\" --limit=200 --format=json | jq '.[] | {time: .timestamp, actor: .protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, method: .protoPayload.methodName, resource: .protoPayload.resourceName}'```

Morgan: Quick sample output (sanitized):
- time: 2025-11-02T03:12:11Z actor: legacy-builder@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com method: Encrypt resource: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/wrap-keys/cryptoKeys/wrap-v1
- time: 2025-11-02T03:13:05Z actor: unknown-service@gcp.iam.gserviceaccount.com method: Decrypt resource: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/wrap-keys/cryptoKeys/wrap-v1

Ana: Oof. We rotated wrap-v1 last month and migrated most services to wrap-v2. Those principal emails shouldn't be present. Could be an old CI worker or partner agent still with IAM binding.

Sam: First actions: (1) enumerate IAM bindings for that key, (2) map emails to active identity entries, (3) if they are orphaned, remove binding and open a short-lived embargo to prevent future use.

Sam: Commands:```gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy wrap-v1 --location global --keyring wrap-keys --project redwood-prod --format=json```then```gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding wrap-v1 --member='serviceAccount:legacy-builder@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter' --project redwood-prod --location global --keyring wrap-keys```

Raj: We should not delete the key or revoke for everyone — need a rolling consumer migration plan. Proposal: revoke suspicious members only, then monitor for any errors for 2h, then schedule a rewrap for secrets that used wrap-v1.

Ana: Agreed. Also double-check Vault transit mounts: some older mounts reference wrap-v1 in metadata. Run:```vault list sys/mounts && vault read transit/keys/wrap-v1```We need to ensure Vault isn't auto-using the key. If it is, change config to wrap-v2 before revoking.

Morgan: I checked — two Vault mounts (team/audit and infra/backup) still reference wrap-v1. I'll open PR to update infra/backup to wrap-v2.

vault-bot: Audit indexer: completed indexing 1,342 KMS-related events for range 2025-11-01..2025-11-03. Use `/audit query kms wrap-v1` to view the collection.

Sam: Owners/plan: Morgan -> update Vault mounts PR (ETA 2h). Raj -> run IAM enumeration + prepare revoke commands (ETA 1h). Ana -> run a BQ logs query to list any non-google accounts hitting the key and start a ticket for partner outreach (ETA 3h). I'll be on standby to coordinate the revoke and monitor SLO dashboards (sre-oncall will help).

sre-oncall: I'll add a grafana panel for KMS errors and a synthetic that hits a staging service using wrap-v2 so we can detect regressions quickly.

Raj: One gotcha — some CI artifacts in GCS are encrypted with wrap-v1-wrapped keys. We should not rupture builds. Plan: remove IAM bindings for unknown principals only, do a 2hr watch, then run a rewrap pass for objects that require it (use storage rewrite with new wrapped key).

Morgan: Rewrap playbook notes: 1) list objects: `gsutil ls -L -r gs://backups/* | grep -E 'KMS key: wrap-v1'` 2) copy/rewrite to same location with `-sse-kms-key` pointing to wrap-v2 3) keep duplicate until verification 4) rotate key's IAM in the end.

Ana: Security question — do we want to accelerate rotation of wrap-v1's key material (create wrap-v3) or just migrate consumers to wrap-v2 and retire wrap-v1 slowly?

Sam: Prefer create wrap-v3 only if we discover active legitimate consumers that can't be updated quickly. Otherwise migrate -> revoke old principals -> deprecate. Creating new key material adds complexity to rewrap.

Morgan: OK — consensus: no forced key re-creation for now. We'll remove suspicious IAM bindings this afternoon after PRs land, watch logs for 2h, then schedule rewrap sweep next day for any remaining ciphertexts.

Raj: I'll capture exact revoke command and post in the incident ticket before executing. Also doing a quick audit to ensure no service account impersonation gaps in IAM condition config.

Sam: Linking runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-orphaned-grants (contains revoke checklist, verification queries, and rollback steps).

Morgan: Thanks all — marking follow-ups: Morgan (Vault PR), Raj (IAM revoke + audit), Ana (BQ partner outreach), Sam (coordinate revoke + monitoring). Will update ticket #SEC-2025-412 with timestamps. :thumbsup:
